summary: Germany tenders large volumes of wind and solar under the Renewable Energy Sources Act, with a sliding market premium that lenders accept, and corporate PPAs are growing. Slow permitting and grid bottlenecks are the main obstacles.

access.reason: The Federal Network Agency regularly tenders large wind and solar volumes under the Renewable Energy Sources Act, and offshore sites are tendered with grid access included.

terms.reason: Auction winners receive a sliding market premium that stabilises revenue and is accepted by banks and development lenders.

ownership.reason: There are no restrictions on moving capital, foreign exchange earnings or dividends.

build.reason: Lengthy approvals and bottlenecks in grid expansion and connection remain major obstacles, despite acceleration measures.

stability.reason: Targets of 80% renewable electricity by 2030 and 70 GW offshore wind by 2045 are set in law, and no retroactive cut was found.

direction.reason: Tendering continues under the existing framework, and no major change was found in the period reviewed.

access.reason: Corporate power purchase agreements are gaining importance for projects outside the support scheme, mainly solar and onshore wind.

ownership.reason: No restrictions on moving capital or dividends.

build.reason: Grid connection delays and limited storage hold back new installations.

stability.reason: Renewable targets are set in law, and no retroactive change to corporate buying was found.

direction.reason: No change to corporate buying rules was found in the period reviewed.

sources.title: Germany Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Buyer credit, curtailment compensation and C&I contract terms were not covered by the sources reviewed.
